summary: Anna Sawerthal is a scholar in Tibetology. She earned an MA at the University of Vienna, supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and completed her PhD at Heidelberg University under doctoral supervisors Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer.

Anna Seidel (1938–1991) was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the universities of Munich and Hamburg and under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf A. Stein. She joined the EFEO in 1969 and worked at the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1970–1991).

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and earned her Ph.D. at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, where she was a research fellow (~1978–1989). She later served as professor at UCLA (~1990–1998) and New York University (~1999).

Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University by 2007 under doctoral supervisors Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.

Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and a PhD at the University of Virginia (~1974–1981). Around 1990, she became Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University.

Anne Casile is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. Her posts include AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (attested 2009) and a position at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development.

Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who completed her degrees at Harvard University (~1982–1997). She taught religious studies at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) before becoming professor of South Asian Religions at Harvard in 2002.

Anne Feldhaus is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Manhattanville College (~1967–1971) and earned her doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). In 1981, she joined Arizona State University, serving as Distinguished Foundation Professor and Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1993–1999), and held an editorial board post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who pursued graduate studies at the University of Chicago (~1989–1996). She served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001–2005).

Anne MacDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida. She held posts at the University of Vienna (attested 2008) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012).

Anne Nishimura Morse is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology who earned her PhD at Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield. She held posts at Smith College (1988–1989) and as a visiting scholar at the Tokyo, Nara, and Kyoto national research institutes and museums.

Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Charles Hallisey. She held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2007).
Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf A. Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist. She studied at the University of Hamburg (~1956–1961), Aix-Marseille University (~1957–1958), and the University of Bonn in 1969.

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) was a religious studies scholar who earned doctorates from Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg. She held professorships at Marburg (1946; 1953–1954), Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1930), later holding posts there (~1935–1944) and as a professor at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1966).

Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1947–1952) and earned a PhD from Somerville College, Oxford (1952). She held faculty posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and earned a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna by 2002, studying under David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian who earned a PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1989–1994) and her Habilitation at MLU Halle-Wittenberg (2008). She held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, the International Association of Sanskrit Studies, and Humboldt University.
